- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.2) — add 3–7% to forecast to avoid bottoming too early.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes — cap forecast at 1–2% below the immediate prior peak.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3 consecutive forecast days exceed true outcome by >5%, adjust downward by 1–3% per day.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops sharply 2–3 days before forecast, reduce forecast slope downward by 1–2% per day.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in the cycle — reduce first 5–7 days by 2–4% if sentiment is rising.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — if sentiment is rising but price is falling, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overreacting to sentiment.
